report.summary: The select fix is built, passes every test, and its negctl arms catch their sabotages. On Windows and in AlmaLinux 8 (OCLJ_GLIBC_MAX=2.28), compiled select(k, ...) now gives the same results and raises the same errors as -joff, under 15 option sets. The fix is in native/luajit/patch-bitop-record.sh, as new hunks 4 and 5. It adds two things to rec_varg. First, a guard before the shift on path C (k beyond the varargs): unsigned k-1 < 2^27, so 1 <= k <= 2^27 or the trace exits. Second, a record-time abort (goto nyivarg) when the recorded k is above 2^27. The main session's reading of the source holds: no path loads through a wrapped index. But the bug has two more classes than the 8k wrap, both now covered and both measured on the shipped build. The first is a k <= 0 in a call with fewer arguments than the function has fixed parameters. The second is a k wrapped by narrowing's unchecked ADD or SUB, on either side of int32. A guard of k >= 1 alone would not fix it: built as a variant, it still differed from -joff in 11 of 15 option sets. Only lj_record.o changes (80 objects compared, both platforms). run-bitjit.sh passes all five parts with PUC on both platforms. run-bitop, run-bitfuzz and nine other runners pass. negctl-bitop.sh with OCLJ_NEGCTL_ARMS=SELGUARD,SELRECK passed four times, canon and restore included. The new suite fails on build/native on both platforms. The smoke timing was NOT run: java.exe was running (PIDs 51272, 51148). A timing script for the main session is ready and its refusals were seen to fire. The full 32-arm negctl sweep is left to the main session.
findings: SOURCE READING CONFIRMED [S] (pristine lj_record.c from git cat-file of the pin, md5 43116dba, rec_varg ~:1989-2088). The main session's three paths are as described. The load (lj_record_vload through an AREF on tridx) is recorded only when 1 <= idx <= nvararg at record time (~:2071), after rec_idx_abc's unsigned ABC on k-1 (~:2059). Path C (~:2061-2070) emits BSHL(k,3)+frofs in 32 bits, the guard LT fr, and no load: tr stays TREF_NIL. Path A with idx > nvararg loads nothing either. So no path loads through a wrapped index. Every test that sent wrapping k to a build without the fix (build/native, SELGUARD, SELRECK, the k>=1-only variant) ran only after this reading.

THE INTERPRETER [M] (probes/interp1-base-joff.txt): lj_lib_checkint reads k with lj_num2int, a plain C (int32_t) cast. On this build every k outside int32 becomes INT32_MIN and raises "index out of range": select(2^31,...), select(2^32+1,...) and select(-2^31-1,...) all raise. Fractions are truncated (2.5 acts as 2, -0.5 as 0, which raises). PUC 5.3.6 differs for k >= 2^31 (returns nothing) and for fractions ("number has no integer representation"), and agrees otherwise (probes/interp1-puc.txt).

MORE DIVERGENCE CLASSES THAN THE 8k WRAP [M] (runs/diag-base-2/jon-classes.txt, on build/native). (1) 8k wrapping past the frame: k = -2^29+20, -2^31+20 (selbug's -2147483628), -2^31 and their kin. (2) No wrap at all: in a call with m' < 0 varargs (fewer arguments than fixed parameters), fr < frofs, so k = 0 and k = -1 passed path C and gave nil. (3) Narrowing wrap [S: lj_opt_narrow.c]. narrow_conv_backprop takes only int16 constants (checki16), and narrow_conv_emit leaves the outermost ADD/SUB unchecked for INDEX conversions. So select(x + 1000, ...) with x + 1000 past 2^31 wrapped to just above -2^31 and gave nil. select(x - 1000, ...) with x - 1000 = -2^31-1 wrapped to 2^31-1 and gave nil in a call with 2 fewer arguments than parameters (3 cases: p2-B/C-am-p, p2few-C-am-p). The interpreter raises in every one of these. Not affected: a constant beyond int16, which is never narrowed (only one guarded CONV), and i + C with i the int loop index, which the recorder emits as ADDOV, a checked add that exits on overflow (probes/iap1-base.dump).

THE FIX'S DESIGN [S][M]. The guard is ULT(k-1, 2^27), unsigned, one line. It exits for every k <= 0 and for every k > 2^27, which includes every narrowing-wrapped k: those lie within 2^15 of +-2^31. After it, 8k+frofs <= 2^30 + 1619 (numparams <= LJ_MAX_LOCVAR 200; the comment uses the looser LJ_MAX_SLOTS bound) and cannot wrap. 2^27 > LUAI_MAXSTACK (65500), so no k within the varargs is refused. A guard of k >= 1 alone, built as a variant in scratch (var-gt0), still differed from -joff in 11 of 15 option sets, 1-3 cases each, all from the am source (runs/bitjit-sel-gt0-2, rc 1). The ULT guard differed in 0 of 15. The guard sits directly before the BSHL; nothing between it and k adds a snapshot (S1), and it exits through the same snapshot as path C's own LT guard (S8).

k >= 2^28 [S][M]. For an exact int32 k >= 1, any pass of upstream's path-C guard gives nil, and nil is right because k > m' (m' <= 65500). Wrapping only turned some passes into exits. So the nil was already right for exact k. The only wrongly passing positive k were narrowing-wrapped ones, which are not the interpreter's k (class 3 above). With the fix, every k in (2^27, 2^31) exits on path C, and a recorded k above 2^27 aborts. Values do not change; such loops run in the interpreter.

THE CONSTANT PATH'S C OVERFLOW (the question asked) [S][M]. Yes: on path A (a constant k beyond the varargs), frofs+8*(int32_t)idx is int arithmetic. It overflows, which is undefined in C, for idx > (2^31-1-frofs)/8: from 2^28-2 with no fixed parameters, from about 2^28-202 at most. What follows on the shipped build: gcc wrapped it. For a constant select(2^28, ...) in f(n, ...) (frofs 27), trace 1 holds 'LT 0014 -2147483621', which always fails. It exits every iteration and grows a chain of side traces, 26 trace starts for two 300-iteration loops; the values are still right (probes/konst1-base.dump, konst1-base.jv). No constant case in t_select differed from -joff on build/native in any option set. With the fix, the record-time abort (idx > OCLJ_SELECT_KMAX) runs before that expression, so it can no longer overflow. The probe then shows 'NYI: bytecode VARG' aborts and the same values (konst1-b2.jv).

findings: RANK 1, belongs in the select round, same branch, same fix. [S] rec_varg's idx > nvararg branch (lj_record.c:2061-2070, export) guards `LT fr, (tridx<<3)+frofs` and loads nothing. fr - frofs is 8*(nargs - numparams), and that difference goes negative when a vararg function gets fewer arguments than it has fixed parameters. Upstream's own code expects this: the on-trace path clamps `if (nvararg < 0) nvararg = 0` (:1997), and the idx <= nvararg branch adds `GE tmp, 0` when numparams is nonzero (:2054-2055); the idx > nvararg branch adds no such guard. So with no wrap at all, a runtime k <= 0 passes the guard whenever nargs - numparams < k (e.g. numparams 2, nargs 0, k = -1 or 0), and the trace returns nil. The interpreter raises 'index out of range' for both (lib_base.c:252-264: i<0 becomes n+i, then i<1 raises) [S][I, not measured]. Proposed value-level differential; it reaches no load: `local K; local function f(a, b, ...) local r; for i = 1, 100 do r = select(K, ...) end; return r end`; record with K = 100 and f(1,2,3,4,5) called a few times; then K = -1 with pcall(f), and K = 0 with pcall(f, 1). Compare JIT on against -joff under the guide's 11.3 option sets. A fix that exits for every runtime k <= 0 (the task's minimum) covers this too.

RANK 2, small enough for the select round. [S] Constant-k branch, lj_record.c:2049-2051: `frofs+8*(int32_t)idx` is int arithmetic in C, so a constant k >= 2^28 is signed overflow, which is undefined behaviour. Neither LuaJIT's src/Makefile nor ../Makefile mentions -fwrapv or -fno-strict-overflow [S]; I did not check build-native.sh's XCFLAGS. What follows, by reading: such a k is always > nvararg, because a frame's varargs are bounded by the Lua stack [I]. So this is the LT guard with no load, and nil is the right answer whenever that guard passes. If the product wraps, the guard can only become an exit that always fires (a speed cost, not a value change) [S][I]. The idx <= nvararg (GE) side never overflows, since there idx <= nvararg is small [S]. Cheapest fix in the same hunk: compute the constant in int64 and refuse to record (or take the variable path) for a constant idx above a bound such as 2^20. Value test, which reaches no load: a literal `select(268435457, ...)` and `select(536870913, ...)` in a hot vararg loop, compared with -joff (nil both ways expected).

RANK 3, confirms the main session's reading, in the select round's fix. [S] Variable-k idx > nvararg branch: 8k is computed in 32 bits (IR BSHL then ADD). For k >= 2^28 the wrapped guard either exits or passes, and nil is correct either way because k exceeds any real nvararg [S][I]. Only k <= 0 diverges: a large negative k through the wrap (P54), and a small k <= 0 through RANK 1. Our fork adds one more way in: since the CRC32 round, a bit result that the table-index fold bounds at 32 bits reaches rec_varg's `CONV int.num INDEX` without its guard. I did not read oclj_bitop_fold.c in this session; this comes from guide 1.2 and 8.8 [I]. Its int value equals the interpreter's, so it is a route to the same divergence, not a new one. t_idx2 can feed select bit results once the fix lands (row 213's note).
